references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus uses the same image of the bridegroom's friends who cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them.
Parallel passage in Mark where Jesus asks the same rhetorical question about wedding guests not being able to fast as long as the bridegroom is among them.
John the Baptist refers to himself as the friend of the bridegroom and points to Jesus as the bridegroom, confirming the image Jesus uses in Luke 5:34.
Isaiah uses the image of the bridegroom rejoicing over his bride as a picture of God's relationship with His people – background for Jesus' self-identification as the bridegroom.
The Lord is referred to as Israel's husband, a fundamental Old Testament image that Jesus connects to when He calls Himself the bridegroom.
Hosea uses the marriage metaphor for God's relationship with Israel, where the Lord betroths His people – background for the bridegroom image Jesus employs.
The wedding of the Lamb in Revelation shows the eschatological fulfillment of the bridegroom image that Jesus introduces about Himself in Luke 5:34.
Paul uses the bridegroom image concerning Christ and the church – he has betrothed the church to Christ as a pure virgin, building further on Jesus' self-understanding as the bridegroom.
Christ as the bridegroom for the church is unfolded here, continuing the bridegroom metaphor that Jesus Himself uses in Luke 5:34.
